faq: What do I get at the end?
A spreadsheet of everything that fires on your site, with a status for each, screenshots as proof and a ranked list of fixes. Premium adds the changes themselves and a retest.
Will you change anything in my accounts during the audit?
No, not in Basic or Standard. We only look and test. In Premium we make the fixes you approve and log each one, so changes can be reversed if needed.
Is the audit useful for a site that is brand new?
Yes, it can stop mistakes before they feed bad data into months of reports. For a new site we also check that the basics are installed in the right place.
How is this different from Data Cleanup?
The audit finds and ranks problems. Data Cleanup repairs deeper issues in reports and history. Many people start with the audit, then pick the fixes that matter to them.
add: Audit a second site or store
desc:
A website tracking audit and fix list shows what your store really measures today, what is broken and what to repair first. Ecom Swift LLC inspects every tag, pixel and event, tests it and hands you a clear, ordered sheet.

## What is a tracking audit?

A tracking audit is a structured check of everything that records visitor activity on your site: analytics, ad pixels, conversion events and the tags that carry them. Each item is tested and marked as working, broken, duplicated or missing. The result is a list of facts, not opinions.

It comes before more tracking, not after. Adding new pixels on top of faulty ones makes the picture worse. A short audit tells you what you already have, so you spend effort on the repairs that matter.

## Why checking your tracking pays off

Tracking fails quietly. A theme update can remove a purchase event, an app can add a second analytics tag, and a checkout change can stop pixels from firing. Everything keeps looking normal, and the reports fill with plausible but wrong numbers. You may only notice months later, after decisions were made on bad data.

An audit catches this early. It also protects your ad spending, since campaigns learn from the events you send. If the purchase event is missing, the platform cannot learn from your buyers. If it fires twice, the platform believes campaigns perform better than they do.

For a store that works with agencies or freelancers, an audit also shows what was left behind and who set it up.

## What a thorough audit covers

- A full inventory of tags, pixels and scripts that load on key pages.
- Tests of the home, collection, product, cart and thank-you pages.
- Checks of analytics events such as view item, add to cart and purchase.
- Checks of ad platform events, using each platform's own test tool.
- A comparison of recent orders with analytics and ad account totals.
- Detection of duplicate tags and duplicate events.
- A look at consent and cookie behavior, where it applies.
- Notes on page weight caused by tracking scripts.
- A status mark for each item, with a plain reason.
- Fixes in priority order, with an estimate of effort.

## How we run the audit

We start in a browser with an inspector open, walking your site as a shopper would. Each page shows which requests fire, with what data. Then we open your analytics and ad accounts to see what arrived on the other side. A tag may fire on the page and still fail to register, and that gap is exactly what we want to find.

Next we place a test order, if you allow it, and follow it through analytics, each ad platform and your store. We compare recent real orders with what each tool recorded, and explain differences.

Finally we write the sheet. Every item gets a status, a description of what we saw and a fix. The Basic package checks core analytics and one ad pixel on key pages. Standard adds the full inventory, up to ten events, order matching and ranked fixes. Premium goes further and makes up to ten fixes in your accounts, checks consent behavior, retests each fix and ends with a review call. Without the fix level, we change nothing in your accounts.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Run an audit before a large ad spend or a theme change.
- Keep the audit document with your other business records.
- Fix the items marked most important first.
- Retest after every repair.
- Ask whoever built your tracking for what they installed.

**Avoid:**
- Adding new pixels before the audit is done.
- Assuming a green tick in a plugin means the event works.
- Fixing items in random order.
- Testing only on the home page.
- Treating one clean check as permanent.

## Who needs a tracking audit

It suits owners who suspect their numbers but cannot say why, and brands about to scale ad spend. It suits stores that changed theme, app set or checkout recently, and buyers or partners who want assurance about a site's data. A very new site can also benefit from a check before launch, since setup mistakes are easier to fix before data starts to pile up.

An audit finds problems and lists fixes. A repair of data that is already wrong is a separate piece of work.

## What we need from you

Your site address, the analytics and ad accounts in use, and access to your store as collaborator or staff. Viewer access is enough for the accounts in the audit levels that make no changes. For the level that includes fixes, we need editor access. We never need your passwords.
